record.original_question: Let G be a graph. Form the inversion graph L(G) whose vertices are all orientations of G, and where two orientations are adjacent when one can be obtained from the other by choosing a set X of vertices and reversing every arc whose two ends both lie in X. What is the diameter of L(G)? In particular, is it always true that diam(L(G)) ≤ Δ(G), where Δ(G) is the maximum degree of G?

evidence.quote: For a digraph D and a subset X of vertices of D, the inversion of X, is the digraph obtained from D by inversing all the the arcs of D with both ends in X.
From a graph G, link two orientations of G if you can pass from one to the other by the inversion of a set. Build like that the inversion graph L (G) of G on all the orientations of G.
What is the diameter of L (G) ? Do we have diam(L (G)) ≤ ∆(G) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. An orientation of $G$ is an assignment of a direction to each edge of $G$, producing an oriented graph (digraph with no 2-cycles). For an oriented graph $D$ and a subset $X\subseteq V$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph obtained from $D$ by reversing every arc whose two endpoints both lie in $X$.

Define the inversion graph $\mathcal{L}(G)$ as follows: its vertex set is the set of all orientations of $G$, and two orientations $D_1,D_2$ are joined by an edge of $\mathcal{L}(G)$ if and only if there exists a set $X\subseteq V$ such that inverting $X$ in $D_1$ yields $D_2$.

Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$, and let $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{L}(G))$ denote the diameter of $\mathcal{L}(G)$.

(a) Determine $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{L}(G))$ as a function of $G$.

(b) In particular, decide whether the inequality
$$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{L}(G)) \le \Delta(G)$$
holds for every graph $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture diam(L(G)) ≤ Δ(G) was formulated by Havet, Hörsch and Rambaud, who proved the upper bound 2Δ − 1 in general and verified the conjecture for Δ = 3 with computer assistance. Subsequent work has established the bound Δ + log Δ for triangle-free graphs and obtained results relating inversion diameter to treewidth and to 2-edge-colored homomorphisms, but the full conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Diameter of the inversion graph
status_evidence.snippet: Havet, Hörsch and Rambaud prove the inversion diameter is at most 2Δ−1 and conjecture it is at most Δ; verified for Δ=3.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture diam(L(G)) ≤ Δ is stated; only partial bounds and small cases are known.

status_evidence.title: Inversion Diameter and Treewidth
status_evidence.snippet: Progress on bounding the inversion diameter, including for triangle-free graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward the Δ-bound conjecture has been made.

status_evidence.title: Inversion diameter and 2-edge-colored homomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Further bounds on inversion diameter via homomorphism techniques.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains an active open problem with continued partial progress.
